about.title: Design is the center. Everything else helps me see the whole system.
about.lead: That is where I begin: I listen to people, map the real work, separate symptoms from causes, and turn the findings into a direction users understand and a team can build.
about.p1: More than 17 years across visual design, web, enterprise UX, business analysis, and technology give me the range to do that.
about.p2: At Roche and Accenture, research, workflow design, visual communication, facilitation, analysis, and implementation support came together in regulated enterprise work. Standing Pillars is my personal portfolio of that path, with Senior UX/Product Design as the central professional focus.
about.personalText: Psychology, anthropology, and sociology help me understand the interpersonal side of problems and what remains unsaid. Outside work, I am a husband and father; I follow astronomy and enjoy films, series, and games.

about.signal: I am most interested in the moment when everyone knows something is not working, but no one can yet say exactly why.
about.principle1Desc: What people do not say often reveals more precisely where a process is actually getting stuck.

about.principle3Title: I carry the idea through delivery
about.principle3Desc: Design does not end with a screen handoff. I support implementation, quality checks, and the communication of decisions.

aiEngineering.title: A work-in-progress engine built through structured AI collaboration
aiEngineering.desc: Tiny Humans Engine is a personal 2D engine and editor prototype. It is a work-in-progress project demonstrating requirements definition, modular architecture, validation, documentation, and responsible use of AI in a complex build.
aiEngineering.projectSub: Work-in-progress 2D engine and editor prototype developed through AI-assisted collaboration
aiEngineering.projectDesc: Tiny Humans is a 30,000+ line personal prototype with an editor, runtime, asset pipeline, scripting system, and packaging work. I used AI tools within a structured loop: Specify -> Architect -> Govern -> Validate. The project demonstrates how I define requirements, manage dependencies, test persistence, and document decisions. It is not a commercially released or production product.
aiEngineering.detailArchDesc: Engine Registry + Event Bus pattern decouples 29 systems. Modular design means any system (lighting, audio, NPCs, scripting) can be developed, tested, and updated independently.
aiEngineering.detailValDesc: A Save Validator checks seven categories of data integrity. A Feature Manifest reduces duplicate work, while persistence checklists support write, read, and round-trip verification.
aiEngineering.detailGovDesc: Project-specific AI instructions define persistence checks, common bug prevention, architecture rules, and implementation workflows. Outputs are reviewed and tested rather than accepted automatically.
aiEngineering.detailProdDesc: Ray-cast lighting with DDA shadows. AI state machines with faction targeting. 4-channel spatial audio. Scene management with map caching. 8-type logic gates with loop prevention. A full scripting SDK with Runtime API.
aiEngineering.method1Desc: Define requirements with the precision of an RFP - scope, constraints, success criteria, integration points.
aiEngineering.method2Desc: Design the system before writing code. Registry patterns, event flows, data models, persistence paths.
aiEngineering.method3Desc: Copilot instructions, feature manifests, validation checklists. The AI follows rules, not vibes.
aiEngineering.method4Desc: Save validators, round-trip testing, documented decisions. Every change is traceable and defensible.
aiEngineering.ctaText: This project does not replace professional engineering experience. It shows how I use structured AI collaboration, verification, and documentation to explore a technically complex personal idea.
aiEngineering.ctaConnects: It is supporting evidence of systems thinking, persistence, and hands-on prototyping.
aiEngineering.progressDesc: The prototype contains 29 major systems, but the broader editor and SDK concept is approximately 15% complete. The proof of concept below is a small extract of about 1,800 lines.

simulationDemo.title: A proof of concept from the engine
simulationDemo.desc: Two autonomous NPCs wander a small tile map in this proof of concept extracted from the engine. No scripts, no rails - just sprite animation, collision detection, weather, and the occasional existential thought bubble. A tiny slice (~1,800 lines) of the 30K+ line engine, running live.

rca.title: Root Cause Analysis Investigation Platform - Manufacturing QA
rca.role: UX Design Lead & Business Analyst · Supported by UI designers
rca.summary: Led UX work for an investigation platform designed for an internal audience of more than 10,000 users. The work translated specialist research and methods such as Fishbone, Is/Is Not, and 5 Whys into guided, traceable workflows.
rca.overviewP1: Enhanced root cause analysis processes within Roche's quality assurance framework. The platform guides manufacturing scientists and investigators through systematic problem-solving methodologies when investigating unplanned events in pharmaceutical production.
rca.contrib1: Modular Interface (Atomic Design) - Implemented Atomic Design principles for a scalable, reusable UI component framework
rca.contrib2: Fishbone Methodology UI - Designed an interface integrating the Ishikawa diagram approach for identifying root causes of manufacturing problems
rca.contrib3: Is/Is Not Analysis UI - Built a tool distinguishing specific problem conditions by comparing scenarios where the problem does and does not occur
rca.contrib4: 5 Whys Interface - Created an intuitive tool guiding investigators through iterative "why" questions to drill down to underlying causes
rca.contrib5: Investigation Modal - Designed the UI for gathering additional information from investigators during the investigation process
rca.contrib6: Comprehensive Process Mapping - Systematically identified and addressed inefficiencies in existing RCA processes
rca.contrib7: Stakeholder Analysis & Advocacy - Conducted in-depth research to inform and advocate for system improvements
rca.contrib8: Change Management - Applied change management theories to guide project evolution across the organisation
rca.methFishboneDesc: Visual cause-and-effect diagram interface for categorising potential causes of manufacturing problems into systematic groupings.
rca.methIsIsNotDesc: Comparative analysis tool distinguishing specific problem characteristics by examining where, when, and how the issue does and doesn't occur.
rca.meth5WhysDesc: Sequential questioning interface that guides investigators through iterative layers of causation to reach the true root cause.
rca.galleryNote: Created in Figma during product development. All displayed names, avatars, IDs, and scenario content are fictionalized. Click an image to enlarge.
rca.outcomeP1: The platform was delivered for an intended internal audience of more than 10,000 users. My contribution established reusable interface patterns and translated several investigation methods into guided workflows in collaboration with subject-matter experts and implementation teams.

iphonePage.barText: Portfolio piece · iPhone 7 Pre-order Landing Page · 2016
iphonePage.noteResearch: Research & Strategy - The iPhone 7 was an iterative update. Market analysis indicated that consumer purchase decisions would hinge primarily on storage capacity rather than incremental hardware improvements such as camera resolution. This insight became the core design driver: surface only the information that matters at the point of conversion - model, colour, and gigabytes.
iphonePage.noteDesign: Design Decisions - Apple's Croatian partner supplied official design guidelines. I deliberately deviated from them. Instead of feature-heavy layouts, the interface was reduced to minimal circular buttons representing storage tiers, with hover states that reflect each phone's actual finish colour. The black background was chosen to complement the cinematic hero video and establish a premium, editorial tone - letting the product imagery carry the visual weight.
iphonePage.noteOutcome: Outcome - Awarded 'Best Promotional Landing Page' in Croatia (Appcom / Apple Partner, 2016). The page contributed to the highest national iPhone 7 pre-order sales for the retailer.
iphonePage.heritageNote: The product copy below remains in its original Croatian. This page was hand-coded in 2016 - every pixel placed with intention, every word chosen in the language it was sold in. Some things are better left as they were made.
iphonePage.footer: Landing page designed and developed by Igor Pilicic, 2016.
